title: 3D Rendering Birmingham: Product, Jewellery, CGI | 22 Signals
description: 3D rendering for Birmingham manufacturers, jewellers, brands and developers: photoreal product, jewellery, packaging and architectural visuals from CAD.
h1: 3D rendering Birmingham makers and manufacturers use instead of a studio shoot
intro: We create photoreal 3D renders for Birmingham businesses: products and components from CAD, jewellery in every metal and stone option, packaging, campaign visuals, and interior and architectural visualisation. We also prepare 3D models for websites and ads. You get images that look like photography, for products that may not exist yet, in every variant you sell.

sections.h: Why photography is not always the answer
p: Photography needs the finished thing. A West Midlands manufacturer launching a new component at a trade show often has a CAD model months before the first production part. A Jewellery Quarter jeweller selling a ring in four metals and six stones cannot make and photograph 24 versions. A developer marketing flats off-plan has nothing built to shoot.
3D rendering solves all three. From a model, we produce images that look like studio photography, in any angle, colour or configuration, and we can change them later without a reshoot.

list: Photoreal product renders: hero shots, white-background catalogue images and detail close-ups.
Packaging: renders of boxes, labels and retail displays before anything is printed.
Campaign visuals: products placed in styled scenes for ads, social and print.
Interior and architectural visualisation for residential, commercial and retail spaces.
3D models for web and ads: optimised files for product viewers, configurators and augmented reality.
Animated turntables and short clips, with full product and technical animation available from our animation team.

p: Many jewellers in Birmingham's Jewellery Quarter already design in CAD before casting. Those same files can produce renders good enough for a website, a customer approval or an Instagram launch. For bespoke commissions, a customer sees exactly how their ring will look in their chosen metal and stone before anything is made. For collections, every variant can be shown online without making stock to photograph it.

Metal, stone and light are some of the hardest things to render convincingly. We spend the time on reflections, facets and surface finishes, because a render that looks like plastic does more harm than no image at all.

sections.h: Renders that work in ads and on product pages
p: A render made for a print catalogue is not automatically right for a Meta ad or a Shopify product page. Ads need bold crops that read on a phone in a split second; product pages need consistent angles, true colour and fast-loading files; trade show graphics need very high resolution.

We plan the output list at the start so one set of models produces every format. That is where 3D rendering Birmingham retailers and manufacturers commission from us tends to pay back: the same model keeps producing new images each season, for new campaigns and new variants, without another shoot.

Design files are often your most valuable intellectual property, especially for automotive suppliers working under customer confidentiality agreements. We sign an NDA before receiving files, store them with restricted access, use them only for the agreed renders, and return or delete them at the end of the project if you ask. If a customer's contract limits who may see a part, tell us and we will work within it.

faqs.q: What can 3D rendering Birmingham businesses commission from you be used for?
faqs.a: Websites and e-commerce, catalogues, packaging approval, ads and social posts, trade show graphics, tenders, investor decks and property marketing. The same model can produce still images, animations and interactive 3D files, so one project can cover several uses.

faqs.q: Can you render jewellery from our CAD files?
faqs.a: Yes. Many Jewellery Quarter jewellers design in CAD, and those files can produce photoreal renders in every metal and stone option. We focus on realistic reflections, facets and finishes so the renders look like photography, for websites, commission approvals and social launches.

faqs.q: Do we need CAD files to get renders?
faqs.a: No, though they help. Without CAD, we can model from technical drawings, measurements, reference photos or a physical sample. Modelling from scratch takes longer, so we confirm what you have and include it in the scope and timeline.

faqs.q: How do you protect confidential designs?
faqs.a: We sign an NDA before receiving files, restrict access to the people working on the project, use files only for the agreed renders, and delete or return them on request. We work within any confidentiality terms your own customers set.

faqs.q: Do you work with Birmingham clients in person?
faqs.a: When the project needs it, for example to inspect a physical sample or match a finish. The rendering itself runs through review links you can comment on directly, with each round confirmed in writing.

faqs.q: Can renders replace product photography completely?
faqs.a: For many uses, yes: catalogue images, variants, packaging and products not yet made. For lifestyle shots with real people, photography or a mix of both often works best. We recommend the right approach for each image rather than rendering everything by default.

faqs.q: How long does a 3D rendering project take?
faqs.a: It depends on whether CAD files exist, how many products and variants are needed and how complex the materials are. A few renders from clean CAD are quick; a full jewellery collection or a styled campaign takes longer. We set out every date in the written scope before starting.
